thin: Small sample ({n} matches): treat it as an anecdote, not a trend.

words.middle: right in the middle of its league

perf.title: How does it compare with its league?
perf.axis: Each bar says where the figure sits in its league; the grey mark is the league's middle. On the right, the place in words.
perf.read: {team}: its best is {best} ({bestWords}) and its weakest, {worst} ({worstWords}). Compared with {teams} teams of its league, over {n} matches.
perf.one: {team}: in {fig}, {words}. Compared with {teams} teams of its league, over {n} matches.
perf.none: {team}: there are not enough figures yet to compare it with its league.

states.title: How long does it lead, draw or trail?
states.axis: The bar splits the minutes played: green leading, grey level, red trailing.
states.read: {team} has spent {won} minutes leading, {level} level and {lost} trailing, over {n} matches.

pulse.title: In which minutes does it score more than its league?
pulse.axis: Horizontal: minute of the match. Vertical: goals per 90 minutes, 100 = its league's average. The light band shows how much the figure could change with other matches.
pulse.readFor: {team} scores {pct} % more goals than its league's average in {slot}, its best stretch, and {low} is when it scores least. Based on {n} matches.
pulse.readAgainst: {team} concedes {pct} % more goals than its league's average in {slot}, its worst stretch. Based on {n} matches.
pulse.flat: {team} does not beat its league's average in any stretch of the match. Based on {n} matches.
pulse.note: Only goals with a minute count. It is the team's history, not what is happening in the match now.

intervals.title: When do its goals come?
intervals.axis: Horizontal: stretch of minutes. Vertical: goals; above, those it scores, below, those it concedes, and the grey mark is what its league's average would be.
intervals.read: In {slot}, {team} scores {gf} goals and concedes {ga}; its league's average in that stretch, over the same matches, would be {lf} scored. In all, {tf} for and {ta} against in {n} matches.

survival.title: How long until the match opens?
survival.axis: Horizontal: minute of the match. Vertical: matches still 0-0 at that minute (%). The dashed line is its league's average.
survival.read: In half of {team}'s matches there is already a goal by minute {median}; {half} % are still 0-0 at half-time. Over {n} matches.
survival.none: More than half of {team}'s matches never open: still 0-0 at the end. Over {n} matches.

xg.title: Does it create more chances than it concedes?
xg.axis: Horizontal: matches, oldest to newest. Vertical: xG per match (average of the last 5).
xg.read: In its latest matches, {team} creates {xf} xG per match and concedes {xa}.
xg.empty: No xG data for this league.

halves.title: Does it score more in the first or the second half?
halves.axis: Two bars per half: goals for and against.
halves.read: {team} has scored {f1} goals in the first half and {f2} in the second; it has conceded {a1} and {a2}. Data from {n} matches.

radar.title: What is its profile against its league?
radar.axis: Six aspects of the game, always in the same order. Each says where the team sits in its league (100 = the best).
radar.read: {team}: its strongest aspect is {best} ({bestWords}) and its lowest, {worst} ({worstWords}).
radar.how: Attack = xG for per match · Finishing = goals minus xG · Volume = shots per match · Presence = corners for minus against · Defence = how few chances it concedes · Discipline = how well it avoids cards

trends.title: What repeats in its matches?
trends.axis: Each row: in how many of its matches it happened. The light stretch is what it could really be with this sample.
trends.read: {team}: what differs most from its league is “{label}”, in {pct} % of {n} matches; in its league, {league} %.
